reviews.title: Causes headphones to crash.
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Useless with an iPhone
reviews.text:
Every time i turn the headphones on they connect to my Mac. 

1. Ok so i toggle the connection to Mac off. Next time i switch the headphones on, it still connects to the Mac! And it makes the Mac connection the active one.
The Mac is switched off and nothing is playing on it.

2. Say I'm listening to a book. The next time i put the headphones on, it will play music from the Mac (or it will play nothing) even though the last thing i did was listen to a book on my phone.

3. I'm connected to my phone. I play the book on the audiobook app. I pause it using the headphones. I play it using the headphones. It does not play the book! It just drops my phone at every possible opportunity.

4. Noise cancelling switches off when I'm in calls. That's the most useless noise cancelling I've ever heard of. And no it's not how Bluetooth works because it works as expected on an old windows 10 laptop - when I'm in calls, the noise cancelling is exactly the same as when I'm not in calls on the windows. So it's technically possible but regressed for newer devices/ios.

"TOTAL CONTROL" - I'd love SOME control. At the moment, i have very little control over what will play out even if it will play!

Very frustrating as it used to work perfectly and now it's just badly designed connections!

reviews.title: Expected more
reviews.text:
There are so many adjustments I wish I could program for my headphones through the app. Wish I didn’t even know there was an app ) :

Here are things I suggest 

1) I want voice commands to be mostly on except for the warning of low device battery. Why is it only on and off? This causes battery percentage, mode, device connected, etc to not be verbally acknowledged when changed or turned on. Even being able to restrict the amount of times the low device battery warning is repeated would be nice. 

2) The modes feel useless as well as the recommended name for “customizable” modes. If I can’t customize my desired modes to also be synched with a specific self adjusted EQ what is the point? To signify noise canceling, wind block, and awareness are on and off? Am I able to customize or is it just the limitation of the product? 

3) To take it a step farther, I would suggest the addition if left/right isolation for my version of customizable modes that include mode synched customizable EQ. This means that I should be able to choose which side of the headphone is aware, noise canceling, wind block (right/left) and at what level. When I’m at my desk all interaction comes from my right side while on my left the loud ac blows. 

Overall the physical product stands great by itself. The app placates the expected average consumer wants but does not create a truly satisfying user experience.

reviews.title: Awful firmware updates
reviews.text:
I purchased the Bose QuietComfort Ultra (1st generation) at launch for $400, expecting long-term premium support to match the premium price. For the first year after release in 2023, the headphones worked without issue.

Since launch, however, Bose has released exactly one firmware update, on March 5, 2024. That is the only software support these headphones have received.

After roughly a year of use, the headphones began experiencing multiple software-related problems: the power button works intermittently, the unit shuts off without warning, and other stability issues appear randomly. These are not hardware failures. They are the type of problems that are routinely addressed through firmware maintenance and incremental updates.

Bose has chosen not to do that.

As a result, I am left with a $400 product that is unreliable and frustrating to use. In practical terms, it has become a premium-priced paperweight.

For comparison, I previously owned premium Sony headphones. While Sony’s build quality did not match Bose’s, Sony consistently released firmware updates that fixed bugs, improved stability, and kept the product functional over time. That ongoing support made a real difference.

Bose, by contrast, appears to have shifted focus entirely to the second-generation QuietComfort lineup while neglecting first-generation customers who paid full price. This is disappointing and unacceptable for a brand that markets itself as premium.

reviews.title: Why force a login?
reviews.text: It is such a poor choice from a UX and CX point of view to force people to log in. This app was great to manage my Bose headphone connection - now I need to faff around with login when all I need to do is quickly connect to my work laptop for a call or I just want to switch to my phone. As a customer, what do I get from logging in? What’s the value to me? Zero. Please get rid of the login again.

reviews.title: QC ULTRA. Overly complicated and dysfunctional App.
reviews.text:
Simply trying to turn on noise cancellation seems like a mythical impossibility. Sound mode options have vague, inconclusive explanations with the Noise Cancellation option locked out with a padlock sign on each mode. No clear mode to simply turn on noise cancellation. Cannot see any other use for this app except using it for volume control or seeing the battery levels. You can set your own configured shortcut touch function but the touch pads are so sensitive it struggles to identify the difference between singe tap, double tap, hold or swipe. Every time you touch the buds you get a random response back.
Update. So the “quiet mode” is noise cancellation. Well you could have fooled me. There’s absolutely no difference in noise cancellation whatsoever. Very disappointed with all except the excellent sound quality of the basic earbuds. Should be sold as no-frills but great sound, which is exactly what they are.

reviews.title: After last update it stopped working
reviews.text: It was all good until last update a week ago. I lost all my devices and settings and can’t connect them all back to the app. Very annoying and irresponsible update indeed!

reviews.title: Still so many issues
reviews.text: I don’t get it, there are so many clear issues to fix. My expectation is that when the headphones are connected, they play all audio sent over paired sources. But when I’m watching a movie I can’t play anything from my phone unless I go to the app and explicitly disable the TV source. Why would I need to do this? Just now, when I was playing a movie and locked my phone, the movie continued but the audio cut out and I had to go to the app and toggle the TV source off and back on to stop this behavior, how would anyone know to do this, why does this happen at all and why does it happen only sometimes? There are several of these bugs and there’s been so much time to fix them by now. Older models didn’t even need an app and were more intuitive to use. Plus apart from setting things one time I never need to go in really and change anything at all, so why is an app required?
